title: Combination of an allogenic and a xenogenic bone substitute material with injectable platelet-rich fibrin – A comparative in vitro study
authors: Kyyak S, Blatt S, Pabst A, Thiem D, Al-Nawas B, Hölze F, Kämmerer PW. J Biomater Appl. 2020 Jul;35(1):83-96.
supports: Pre-clinical study from the botiss maxgraft (processed human allograft) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “This in vitro study shows that maxgraft® granules with i -PRF demonstrate greater proliferation, differentiation, and cell-migration properties than Bio-Oss with i-PRF. Therefore, addition of i-PRF to allogeneic bone grafting material may influence osteoblast activity in vivo. Independently of iPRF, maxgraft® seems to have favorable effects on HOB compared to BioOss” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
